tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms.summary: Mathlib already has the analytic foundation plus more than the document credits: the L-function L and completed Lambda of a modular form on an arithmetic group (Mellin transform, an abstract functional equation against f|S, entireness for cusp forms), the norm map, Eisenstein series at level Gamma(N), the level-one Sturm bound and dimension formula, and the Hecke-ring definitions. Tau Ceti has built most of the classical trunk: diamond operators, character spaces and the nebentypus decomposition, the Hecke ring with convolution and commutativity (GL_n and Gamma0(N)), classical T_n with coefficient recurrences and U_p = T_p, the valence formula at level one and at every finite index (Layer 1 is built), the finite-index Sturm bound, the Petersson inner product with the old/new decomposition, bundled good eigenforms and newforms, fixed-space strong multiplicity one and multiplicity one, the per-character Main Lemma, the level-lowering dichotomy, and normalized Atkin-Lehner and Fricke operators. Genuinely missing are Eisenstein series with character and the cusp-Eisenstein decomposition, the j-function, Shimura 3.35 and the p-adic hand-off, Hecke adjoints and eigenbases, bad-prime newform theory (Atkin-Lehner-Li, conductor, cross-level strong multiplicity one), Atkin-Lehner signs, the Euler product and the Fricke-form functional equation, all of modular symbols, coefficient fields, Galois stability and the LMFDB invariants, the modular curve with analytic Riemann-Roch and the general dimension formulas, and the Eichler-Selberg trace formula.

targets.target: Level-one j inputs: normalized j = E4^3/Delta, its SL2(Z)-invariance and q-expansion, j - 1728 = E6^2/Delta, exact orders at rho and i
targets.note: Neither library defines the j-function: grep for 1728 outside Weierstrass curves finds only Delta = (E4^3 - E6^2)/1728, and jFunction/kleinJ/jInvariant hits are WeierstrassCurve.j or knot-theory J. The inputs exist (E4, E6, Delta, the level-one valence formula and its order bound), but no j, no j-invariance or q-expansion, and no exact ord_rho E4 = 1 or ord_i E6 = 1 statement.

targets.target: Diamond operators <d> on M_k(Gamma1(N)) and S_k(Gamma1(N)), independent of the lift, as monoid homs into the endomorphism algebras; Gamma0(N)/Gamma1(N) = (ZMod N)^x
targets.note: Root-namespace declarations; cusp versions diamondOpCusp (line 224) and diamondOpCuspHom (line 267). coe_diamondOp shows <d>f = f|[k]g for any lift g in Gamma0(N). There is no bundled isomorphism Gamma0(N)/Gamma1(N) = (ZMod N)^x; it follows from Mathlib's Gamma1' N := ker Gamma0Map plus the surjectivity lemma.

targets.target: Character spaces M_k(N,chi), S_k(N,chi) as simultaneous diamond eigenspaces (Submodules), with the nebentypus transformation law as a theorem
targets.note: Defined as the infimum over d of Module.End.eigenspace (diamondOpHom k d) (chi d), exactly the AINTLIB shape; the character is a unit hom (ZMod N)^x ->* C^x.

targets.target: Nebentypus decomposition: M_k(Gamma1(N)) and S_k(Gamma1(N)) are internal direct sums of the character spaces
targets.note: Stated as DirectSum.IsInternal under [DecidableEq ((ZMod N)^x ->* C^x)]; the halves iSupIndep_modFormCharSpace and iSup_modFormCharSpace_eq_top are in the same file.

targets.target: Parity lemma M_k(N,chi) != 0 -> chi(-1) = (-1)^k, and the isomorphism M_k(Gamma0(N)) = M_k(N, trivial)
targets.note: The equivalence needs [NeZero N] and preserves the underlying function.

targets.target: Eisenstein series with character E_k^{psi,phi,t} in M_k(N, psi phi), their q-expansions via generalized Bernoulli numbers and twisted divisor sums, E2(z) - t E2(tz), weight one, and the Gauss-sum translation to Mathlib's eisensteinSeries
targets.note: Mathlib has the level-Gamma(N) congruence-class series in weight k >= 3, the level-one q-expansion, E2 and Gauss sums, and Tau Ceti has the twisted divisor sums; missing are the character-twisted series in M_k(N, psi phi), generalized Bernoulli numbers B_{k,chi}, their q-expansions at level N, the weight-2 combination E2(z) - tE2(tz), weight-one Eisenstein series, and the Gauss-sum comparison.

targets.target: Cusp-Eisenstein decomposition M_k(N,chi) = S_k(N,chi) + E_k(N,chi): constant-term maps at all cusps, their common kernel, spanning by Eisenstein series, dimension of the Eisenstein subspace
targets.note: Only level one is done (rank M_k = 1 + rank S_k for even k >= 3, cusp form iff constant term 0), and Mathlib characterizes cusp forms by vanishing at every cusp for HasDetOne groups. There is no Eisenstein subspace at level N, no constant-term maps at all cusps, no complement statement and no Eisenstein dimension.

duplicates.note: Also constructs generalized Eisenstein series with tame nebentypus and their q-expansions (as input to Eisenstein measures).

targets.target: Level-one valence formula over SL2(Z)-orbits with weights 1/2 at i, 1/3 at rho and ord at infinity, = k/12
targets.note: For any ModularFormClass on SL2(Z) with f != 0; the finsum runs over non-elliptic orbits exactly as in the AINTLIB statement.

targets.target: Contour-integral proof inputs: Hungerbuehler-Wasem generalized winding numbers of the fundamental-domain boundary (1/2 at i, 1/6 at each rho-corner)
targets.note: Values are computed for the clockwise boundary (-1/6 at rho and at rho+1, -1/2 on the open arc including i).

targets.target: General-level valence formula for every finite-index Gamma via the full-coset norm map Nm(f) = prod f|[k]gamma
targets.note: Proved for Gamma <= SL2(Z) of finite index with right-hand side k*[SL2(Z):Gamma]/12, interior weights 2*ord/|Stab_Gamma P| (= 1/e_P when -I is in Gamma) and cusp terms indexed by translation orbits on cosets, so a classical cusp may appear as one or two orbits.

targets.target: Order dictionary: orbit-invariance of interior orders, stabilizer orders e_P, rational orders at cusps in the width parameter, finite support of the order divisor at every finite-index level
targets.note: orderAtCusp h f is the Q-valued order read from the q_{2h}-expansion, half-integral at irregular cusps (the errata convention); finite support is proved for [Gamma.FiniteIndex] (public declaration, not in the index).

targets.target: Sturm-bound inequality ord_inf(f) <= k*index/12 for nonzero f at finite index
targets.note: Stated with the full index [SL2(Z):Gamma] (the weaker form when -I is not in Gamma); the projective-index sharpening is not stated separately.

duplicates.note: Names the valence formula's treatment of i and rho as an application of the generalized residue theorem, i.e. the winding-number input of this layer.

targets.target: Hecke ring convolution product, identity and associativity on Mathlib's HeckeRing double-coset objects
targets.note: Mathlib has IsHeckeTriple, HeckeCoset, HeckeCosetModule and HeckeRing (definitions only); Tau Ceti builds the mixed-level convolution, unit and associativity and the Semiring/Ring instances on them (files mark themselves as copies of Mathlib PRs #41277, #41279, #41328).

targets.target: GL_n Hecke pair (SL_n(Z), Delta_n): commutativity via the transpose anti-involution, degree map, elementary-divisor parametrization of double cosets, coprime multiplicativity
targets.note: All at general n with [NeZero n]; explicit degree values are computed only for scalar cosets and for GL2.

targets.target: Shimura Thm 3.20: the p-local Hecke ring R_p is the polynomial ring on T(p,1,...,1), ..., T(p,...,p)
targets.note: Proved only for n = 1 and n = 2 (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) Z = pLocalSubring 2 p); at general n only the combinatorial leading-exponent injectivity exists, not the triangular expansion or generation.

targets.target: Congruence Hecke pairs (Gamma0(N), Delta0(N)) and Gamma1(N); the surjection R(SL2(Z),Delta) -> R(Gamma0(N),Delta0(N)) with kernel generated by T(p,p) for p | N (Shimura 3.35); commutativity at level N via the Atkin-Lehner anti-involution
targets.note: The pairs are IsHeckeTriple instances (Gamma0/Basic.lean:141, Gamma1/Basic.lean:107) and the level-N ring is commutative, but Shimura's Theorem 3.35 (the ring surjection from level one and its kernel) is absent; only the injectivity of the coset map on coprime-determinant cosets (Shimura 3.31) exists.

targets.target: Hand-off to automorphic representations: identification of the p-part with the p-adic Hecke ring of (GL_n(Z_p), M_n(Z_p) cap GL_n(Q_p)) including structure constants, the determinant-sign lemmas, and inverting T(p,...,p)
targets.note: Only the sign lemma 'Smith normal form with positive diagonal by SL_n(Z) changes of basis' exists; there is no p-adic or GL_n(Q) Hecke ring, no comparison of structure constants, no localization at T(p,...,p) and no spherical Hecke algebra or Satake map in either library.

targets.target: Hecke operators T_n as C-linear endomorphisms of M_k(Gamma1(N)) preserving M_k(N,chi) and S_k(N,chi), and the ring homomorphism from the abstract Gamma0(N) Hecke ring
targets.note: The ring homomorphism into End of each character space exists, and heckeTNat acts on all of M_k(Gamma1(N)); but heckeTNat is the single double coset T(1,n), equal to the classical T_n only when no p^2 | n with p coprime to N, and the classical composite T_n exists only on each character space, not as one operator on M_k(Gamma1(N)). Preservation of the character spaces is proved at primes and at level-supported n.

targets.target: q-expansion recurrences: a_m(T_p f) = a_{mp} + chi(p)p^{k-1}a_{m/p}, the general divisor-sum formula, T_mT_n = T_{mn} for coprime m,n, the prime-power recurrence, the general T_mT_n formula
targets.note: The coefficient formulas carry f in modFormCharSpace k chi and Coprime p N as the roadmap asks; the general T_mT_n divisor-sum identity is proved in the abstract Gamma0(N) ring.

targets.target: U_p as an alias with U_p = T_p at p | N, and T_{p^r} = T_p^r at p | N
targets.note: heckeUNat is an abbrev for heckeTNat at a prime p | N, and the alias lemma is rfl.

targets.target: Diamond operators in the Hecke algebra: double cosets in the Gamma1(N)-pair ring, scalar cosets in the Gamma0(N)-pair ring acting on M_k(N,chi), compatibility with the slash-defined diamonds
targets.note: The scalar coset T(c,c) acts on M_k(N,chi) by chi(c)c^{k-2} (the roadmap's 'by chi(d)' omits the power of c).

targets.target: Normalization lemma identifying the double coset of diag(1,p) acting by slash with the classical T_p; Hecke action preserves cuspidality and nebentypus
targets.note: The identification is proved at primes; for composite n the ring element is linked to the operator only through the coefficient formula and a_1(T_n F) = a_n(F).

duplicates.note: Spherical Hecke algebras and the Satake isomorphism for local groups: the p-adic end of the hand-off in (a').
Constructs Hecke correspondences, degeneracy maps and diamond operators algebraically from the moduli interpretation; the analytic operators here are the complex-analytic counterpart.
Hecke correspondences on automorphic bundles with scalar normalizations and composition against the abstract Hecke algebra, which covers the modular-curve case.

targets.target: Petersson inner product on S_k(Gamma) for finite-index Gamma as a positive-definite Hermitian inner product: invariant measure, fundamental domains and independence of choice, convergence from decay at every cusp
targets.note: An InnerProductSpace.Core on CuspForm (Gamma.map (mapGL R)) k for Gamma <= SL2(Z) of finite index, defined as a sum over cosets of Gamma.withCenter of fundamental-domain integrals; integrability comes from Mathlib's CuspFormClass.petersson_bounded_left (Bounds.lean:189) through integrableOn_petersson_fd_left. The Core is a def, not an instance, and the pairing is not normalized by the covolume.

targets.target: Petersson adjoint of good Hecke operators, <T_n f, g> = <f, <n>^{-1} T_n g> for (n,N) = 1, hence T_n* = chi(n)^{-1}T_n on S_k(N,chi) and normality
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the ingredients (diamond operators are Petersson-unitary; slash by g moves to the adjugate on the other side; the coset-union change of variables and fundamental domains of Hecke translates) but never assembles the adjoint formula for T_n, normality, or self-adjointness when chi(n) = 1; 'T_n*' occurs only in docstrings.

targets.target: Simultaneous (orthonormal) eigenbasis of the good Hecke operators
targets.note: grep for eigenbasis, OrthonormalBasis and simultaneous diagonalization in both ModularForms and HeckeRing trees finds only the diamond-operator character decomposition (isInternal_cuspFormCharSpace).

targets.target: Old subspace spanned by level-raises f(d tau) from proper divisor levels, new subspace as its Petersson orthogonal complement, their complementarity and T_n-stability
targets.note: The spaces, V_d with a_n(V_d f) = a_{n/d}(f), and IsCompl are proved; Hecke stability is only 'T_p preserves the old space for primes p coprime to N'. T_n-stability of the new space, and old-space stability for composite good n, are missing.

targets.target: Fixed-character refinement with exact indexing S_k(N,chi)^old = sum over M | N with cond chi | M and d | N/M of V_d S_k(M, chi_M), and S_k(N,chi)^new = S_k(Gamma1(N))^new cap S_k(N,chi)
targets.note: The old/new decomposition restricts to each character space and new cap S_k(N,chi) is the relative orthogonal complement, but the conductor-indexed description of the oldspace by descended characters chi_M is not proved (the Nebentypus.lean docstring says so).

targets.target: Bad-prime stability: the new subspace is stable under U_p for p | N (equivalently <U_p f_new, g_old> = 0), Fricke transport of degeneracy maps and the oldspace, stability of old and new spaces under all Hecke operators (D-S Prop 5.6.2)
targets.note: U_p (heckeUNat/heckeUCuspNat) is used only in HeckeSlash/BadPrime and LevelSupported.lean; the T_p-degeneracy commutation heckeTCuspNat_levelRaise holds only for p coprime to N, and no Fricke or U_p statement touches cuspFormsOld/cuspFormsNew.

targets.target: Good-Hecke eigenform (EigenformAwayFromLevel, with nebentypus and nonzero) and the full all-T_n eigenform notion, with eigenvalue API
targets.note: The bundled good eigenform carries chi, membership in S_k(N,chi), good-index eigenvalues and f != 0; the propositional IsEigenformAwayFromLevel has neither nebentypus nor nonvanishing. The full notion (eigen for every T_n including U_p, D-S Def 5.8.1) is deliberately not ported (Eigenform.lean docstring).

targets.target: Newform structure (new subspace, a_1 = 1, eigen away from the level) and PrimitiveForm
targets.note: Matches the pinned shape (extends EigenformAwayFromLevel with isNew and isNorm); only the PrimitiveForm alias name is not declared.

targets.target: Newforms are full eigenforms (Atkin-Lehner-Li; D-S Thm 5.8.2 / Miyake 4.6.13): eigenvectors of U_p for p | N
targets.note: Only the coefficient criterion for U_p-eigenvectors exists; no theorem makes a Newform a U_p-eigenvector (the Newform.lean docstring records the gap).

targets.target: Bad-prime eigenvalue classification (Miyake 4.6.17): a_p != 0 iff v_p(N) = max(1, v_p(cond chi)), with a_p^2 = chi^{(p)}(p)p^{k-2} or |a_p| = p^{(k-1)/2}
targets.note: Searches for 4.6.17, a_p^2, (k-1)/2 exponents, padicValNat with newforms, and bad-prime eigenvalues find nothing beyond the U_p coefficient criterion.

targets.target: Atkin-Lehner Main Lemma (D-S 5.7.1): a cusp form with a_n = 0 for all n coprime to N is old, in the sharp form f = sum over p | N of iota_p f_p
targets.note: Both the oldness statement and the sharp decomposition f = sum_p V_p F_p with F_p in S_k(Gamma1(N/p)) are proved for f in a character space S_k(N,chi); the statement for an arbitrary f in S_k(Gamma1(N)), obtained from these through the nebentypus decomposition, is not stated.

targets.target: Level-lowering dichotomy (Miyake Thm 4.6.4): if the level raise of a periodic f lies in S_k(N,chi), either chi factors through N/l and f is in S_k(N/l, chi_lowered) or f = 0
targets.note: Hypotheses as in AINTLIB: l | N, chi a DirichletCharacter C N, f : H -> C invariant under T, g in S_k(N,chi) equal to l^{1-k} f|diag(l,1).

targets.target: Newform decomposition (Miyake Cor 4.6.20 / D-S Thm 5.8.3): existence of the associated primitive pair (M, g) with M | N for every normalized good eigenform, and its uniqueness (the conductor)
targets.note: All newform statements are at one fixed level; there is no existence or uniqueness of a primitive associate and no conductor of an eigenform (searches: 4.6.20, 5.8.3, conductor with Newform/EigenformAwayFromLevel).

targets.target: Strong multiplicity one in a fixed space: two newforms of the same level, weight and nebentypus with equal eigenvalues at coprime n outside a finite set are equal
targets.note: Keeps the three hypothesis groups: same N and k in the type, f.chi = g.chi, and a finite exceptional Finset of good indices.

targets.target: Key step: a newform and a good eigenform sharing eigenvalues are proportional (strongMultiplicityOne_constMul)
targets.note: Proportionality is proved only when both forms lie in the new subspace of the same character space; the AINTLIB statement allowing the second form to be an arbitrary (possibly old) good eigenform is not ported.

targets.target: Multiplicity one: each simultaneous good-Hecke eigenspace in S_k(N,chi)^new is one-dimensional
targets.note: Dimension at most one for every eigenvalue system, exactly one once the eigenspace is nonzero.

targets.target: Newforms form an orthogonal basis of S_k(Gamma1(N))^new
targets.note: No basis or orthogonality statement for newforms (it needs the missing Hecke adjoint); only orthogonality of different character spaces exists.

targets.target: Cross-level strong multiplicity one for newforms (Miyake 4.6.19): newforms of levels N, M agreeing at almost all p not dividing NM have N = M, the same nebentypus and are equal
targets.note: Only the fixed-level fact that equal good eigenvalues force equal nebentypus exists; nothing compares newforms of different levels.

targets.target: Coefficient characterization (D-S Prop 5.8.5): f in M_k(N,chi) is a normalized eigenform iff a_1 = 1, the prime-power recurrence and multiplicativity hold
targets.note: The forward direction is proved for newforms at good indices only (m, n coprime to N, p not dividing N), and there are per-prime eigenvector criteria; the two-sided characterization over all n including bad primes is not assembled.

duplicates.note: States strong multiplicity one for GL2 cuspidal automorphic representations, the adelic form of this layer's statements.
Re-uses newform finiteness, Galois conjugation and strong multiplicity one to pin a rational weight-two newform; a consumer that restates the fixed-level statements.

targets.target: Exact divisors Q || N and the Atkin-Lehner operators W_Q for every exact divisor, normalized by (sqrt Q)^{2-k}
targets.note: The operators act on S_k(Gamma0(N)) (trivial nebentypus), where the normalized W_Q is an involution in every weight; the raw W_Q^2 = Q^{k-2} is Operator.lean:344.

targets.target: Normalized Fricke operator (sqrt N)^{2-k}(f|[0,-1;N,0]) on S_k(Gamma1(N)): involution, +-1 eigenspaces, transport of chi-spaces
targets.note: Public declarations (absent from the index). The square is (-1)^k, an involution for even k; the character space of chi is carried to that of chi^{-1}.

targets.target: Relations: W_Q commute with T_n away from Q, W_Q W_R = W_{QR/gcd(Q,R)^2}, action of (Z/2)^{omega(N)}
targets.note: The composition law and the group action (possibly non-faithful) are proved on S_k(Gamma0(N)); commutation of W_Q or the Fricke operator with the Hecke operators T_n is absent (no Hecke operator appears in AtkinLehner/ or Fricke/).

targets.target: Sign theory for trivial nebentypus: W_Q f = eps_Q f with eps_Q = +-1 on newforms, product of prime-power signs = Fricke sign, functional-equation sign i^k eps_N
targets.note: Only the +-1 eigenspace splitting of each normalized W_Q exists; newforms live on Gamma1(N) and are never related to W_Q, and eps_Q appears only in docstrings.

targets.target: General nebentypus: Fricke sends a primitive form to a multiple of its conjugate form (Miyake 4.6.15), Atkin-Li pseudo-eigenvalues of modulus one
targets.note: No conjugate form f_rho and no pseudo-eigenvalue; only the chi -> chi^{-1} space isomorphism exists.

targets.target: Old-space (and new-space) stability under Fricke and W_Q, Fricke conjugation of degeneracy maps
targets.note: Only W_N <d> = <d^{-1}> W_N is proved; no Fricke statement mentions cuspFormsOld, cuspFormsNew or levelRaise.

targets.target: L-function L(s,f) = sum a_n(f) n^{-s} of a modular form, built on Mathlib's LSeries
targets.note: Mathlib defines L (and Lambda) for any ModularFormClass on an arithmetic Gamma with 0 < k, identifying it with the Dirichlet series of the width-h q-expansion up to the factor h^{-s}; Tau Ceti restates this as an LSeries identity. The roadmap's statement that Mathlib has no L-function of a modular form is out of date.

targets.target: Abscissa of absolute convergence <= k/2 + 1 for cusp forms and <= k + 1 for modular forms of weight k >= 0, and the sharpening <= k for non-cusp forms
targets.note: Both proved bounds exist on arithmetic subgroups (Hecke's a_n = O(n^{k/2}) and a_n = O(n^k) for k >= 0 are Mathlib's). The tightened non-cuspidal abscissa <= k (a_n = O(n^{k-1}) resp. O(n^{k-1+eps})) is absent.

targets.target: Euler product L(s,f) = prod_p (1 - a_p p^{-s} + chi(p) p^{k-1-2s})^{-1} for a newform, Re s > k/2 + 1
targets.note: Mathlib's general Euler product for multiplicative arithmetic functions and newform multiplicativity and the prime-power recurrence at good indices exist; the degree-two Euler product itself is absent, and so are the coefficient relations at p | N that it needs.

targets.target: Completed L-function via the Mellin transform of f(iy), Hecke's functional equation with the Fricke companion Lambda_N(k - s, f) = i^k Lambda_N(s, g), entireness and analytic continuation of L(s,f)
targets.note: Mathlib's Lambda comes from a WeakFEPair pairing f(it) with (f|[k]S)(it) and epsilon = i^k, so an abstract functional equation against f|S holds, and Lambda and L are entire for cusp forms (Tau Ceti adds the entire extension of the coefficient L-series). Missing: the level-N completed Lambda_N and the stated equation with the normalized Fricke companion; non-cusp forms get no continuation of L.

targets.target: One-form functional equation with sign i^k eps for Fricke eigenforms (D-S Thm 5.10.2)
targets.note: The Fricke +-1 eigenspaces exist, but no L-function statement uses them and no root number is defined.

targets.target: Analytic rank (order of vanishing of the entire continuation at s = k/2) and analytic conductor (Iwaniec-Kowalski normalization)
targets.note: Only the generic analyticOrderAt exists; searches for analytic rank, analytic conductor and central value find nothing.

duplicates.note: Defines the analytic rank of an elliptic curve as the order of the entire continuation at the centre, via the modular L-function; the same definition specialized to weight two.
Proves the Mellin formula expressing period integrals of a newform through L(f, chi, j+1), overlapping the completed L-function and twists.

targets.target: Modular-symbol module M N k = Gamma1(N)-coinvariants of Div^0(P^1(Q)) tensor Sym^{k-2}(Z^2), a finite Z-module
targets.note: Only generic ingredients exist (coinvariants of a representation, symmetric powers, cusps of SL2(Z) = P^1(Q)); there is no degree-zero cusp divisor module, no modular-symbol module and no finiteness theorem.

targets.target: Manin symbols, SL2(Z) generation and the fundamental-domain boundary presenting the symbol module
targets.note: Generation of SL2(Z) by S and T, the fundamental domain and a truncated boundary contour exist; Manin symbols and the presentation of the symbol module are absent.

targets.target: Hecke action on modular symbols, its commutativity and integrality
targets.note: No Hecke operator acts on any symbol module; searches for modular symbol, Manin and Hecke with symbol find nothing.

targets.target: Period map S_k(Gamma1(N)) -> Hom_Z(M N k, C): raw geodesic pairing, absolute convergence between cusps, Gamma1(N)-invariance, descent, Hecke and diamond equivariance
targets.note: Only the cusp-decay estimate used for convergence exists; no period integrals, period polynomials or cocycles.

targets.target: Injectivity of the period map via the Eichler integral and Bol's identity, including 'bounded invariant function of weight <= 0 is constant'
targets.note: Mathlib proves that modular forms of weight 0 on arithmetic groups are constant and of negative weight vanish (the named sub-theorem once E_f is shown holomorphic and bounded at the cusps), and the slash rule for the normalized derivative; the Eichler integral, the iterated Bol identity and the injectivity theorem are absent.

targets.target: Integral Hecke algebra heckeAlgZ N k (generated by T_n and diamonds) is a finitely generated Z-module, via the free-algebra kernel inclusion
targets.note: The image of the integral Gamma0(N) Hecke ring in End(S_k(N,chi)) is available as a ring hom, but nothing is proved about Z-finiteness of any Hecke algebra (only C-finite-dimensionality of the form spaces).

targets.target: Hecke eigenvalues are algebraic integers and CoefficientField f = Q(a_n) is a number field (k >= 2; weight one via the Deligne-Serre lattice)
targets.note: No coefficient field of a newform, no integrality of eigenvalues, no weight-one lattice; searches for coefficient field, IsIntegral with Hecke eigenvalues and IntermediateField Q C near modular forms find nothing.

targets.target: Vanishing S_k = 0 for k <= 0
targets.note: Negative weight is proved on arithmetic groups; weight-zero forms are constant, but the vanishing of weight-zero cusp forms is not stated.

duplicates.note: Constructs modular symbols on degree-zero divisors of P^1(Q), Manin symbols, Hecke and diamond actions, and the Eichler-Shimura period maps with injectivity - the same machinery as this layer.
Constructs the coefficient field of a newform and saturated integral modular-symbol lattices.
Defines the integral Hecke algebra through a faithful action on a finite module and proves finiteness over the coefficient ring (Jacobian route).
Asks for exact modular symbols and Hecke matrices for computation.

targets.target: CharacterField chi generated by the values of chi, and CharacterField chi <= CoefficientField f for a newform in S_k(N,chi)
targets.note: Only the fact that character values are roots of unity exists; no character field and no coefficient field.

targets.target: Semisimple Hecke-algebra correspondence: after tensoring with C, the characters of the newspace Hecke algebra over Q(chi) are exactly the normalized newforms
targets.note: Multiplicity one and strong multiplicity one are available as inputs, but there is no Hecke algebra over Q(chi) or Q, no semisimplicity and no eigenline correspondence.

targets.target: Galois-conjugate newform f^sigma for embeddings of the coefficient field, a_n(f^sigma) = sigma(a_n(f)), chi_{f^sigma} = sigma o chi, orbit sizes equal to field degrees
targets.note: Only sigma o chi for characters and the generic orbit-size fact for roots of a separable minimal polynomial exist.

targets.target: Rationality: charpoly(T_n | S_k(N,chi)^new) lies in Q(chi)[X] and factors as a product of norms of X - a_n(f); the Q-version over character orbits
targets.note: No rational structure on spaces of modular forms at level N and no Hecke characteristic polynomial.

duplicates.note: Proves rationality of the coefficient field of the weight-two newform attached to E via Galois conjugation and strong multiplicity one, a special case of the conjugate-newform construction.

targets.target: Hecke characteristic polynomials charpoly(T_n | S_k(N,chi)^new), coefficients from traces of powers via Newton's identities, factorization into orbit norms
targets.note: Newton's identities (for MvPolynomial) and the charpoly/trace API exist; no Hecke characteristic polynomial, no charpoly-from-traces-of-powers theorem, no orbit factorization.

targets.target: Satake parameters as the roots of X^2 - a_p X + chi(p)p^{k-1}, and the Satake angle under the Ramanujan-Deligne bound as a hypothesis
targets.note: Only generic quadratic Vieta and discriminant lemmas exist; no Satake parameters, and no Ramanujan-Petersson bound even as a hypothesis.

targets.target: Galois-conjugate forms and orbits over the character orbit (from Layer 8G)
targets.note: Depends on the absent Layer 8G construction; nothing in either library.

targets.target: Twists f tensor psi by Dirichlet characters (modularity, level bound, nebentypus chi psi^2, a_p(f tensor psi) = psi(p)a_p(f)), primitive associates, inner twists and CM self-twists
targets.note: Every 'twist' in the modular-forms trees is the slash action or a nebentypus-weighted Hecke sum; no twisted modular form.

targets.target: Galois-group certification: Galois closure, Dedekind/Frobenius cycle-type certificates, the discriminant square test, the S5 certificate for small degree
targets.note: The discriminant test (monic separable, char != 2), normal closures, full-symmetric-group criteria (prime degree with two non-real roots; transposition plus transitivity in Equiv.Perm) and Frobenius-orbit sizes over finite fields exist; Dedekind's theorem that the factorization mod p gives a Frobenius cycle type in Gal(f/Q), and the certificate checker, are absent.

targets.target: Dual form f-bar and IsSelfDual f iff all a_n are real
targets.note: No conjugate newform and no self-duality predicate.

targets.target: LMFDB labels N.k.a.x, Conrey labels and Galois orbits of Dirichlet characters
targets.note: No labels; Mathlib's lmfdb cross-reference attribute is a docstring-link database, unused in either library.

targets.target: badPrimes f = N.primeFactors
targets.note: badPrimes exists only for Weierstrass curves and ideal weights, not for modular forms.

duplicates.note: States the discriminant test IsSquare f.discr iff the Galois image lies in the alternating group.
States Dedekind's theorem that factor degrees mod p give the Frobenius cycle type, the core of the cycle-type certificates.
Classifies transitive subgroups of S_n for n <= 5 with label predicates, the small-degree Galois-group recognition this layer's certification needs.
LMFDB label and invariant suite for number fields, the coefficient-field side of the labels.

targets.target: Sturm bound at finite index and finite-dimensionality of M_k(Gamma), S_k(Gamma) at every finite-index level; forms agreeing on the first floor(k*index/12)+1 coefficients are equal
targets.note: Proved for Gamma <= GL2(R) of finite relative index in SL2(Z) with discrete strict periods (and HasDetOne for the Module.Finite instances), under the names the roadmap pins; the full index [SL2(Z):Gamma] is used.

targets.target: Concrete dimensions at level > 1: dim S_2(Gamma0(11)) = 1, dim S_2(Gamma0(23)) = 2, dim S_2(Gamma0(2)) = 0, dim M_2(Gamma0(11)) = 2, dim S_2(Gamma1(13)) = 2
targets.note: No explicit dimension is computed at any level above one.

targets.target: The analytic modular curve X(Gamma) for congruence subgroups with cusp and elliptic counts and the degree of X(Gamma) -> X(1) (detailed in 10A)
targets.note: Proper discontinuity, finiteness of cusp orbits and stabilizer orders exist; no compactified curve, no counts, no degree theorem (see 10A).

targets.target: Compact Riemann surface cohomology: H^1 finiteness, analytic Riemann-Roch, Serre duality, genus comparison and dim S_2 = g (detailed in 10B)
targets.note: Only the algebraic Riemann-Roch theorem for function fields exists (see 10B).

targets.target: Dimension formulas for M_k(Gamma) and S_k(Gamma) at general level, even and odd weight (detailed in 10C)
targets.note: Only level one and the trivial weights k <= 0 are done (see 10C).

duplicates.note: Requires Sturm-style truncation bounds before declaring forms equal, the computational use of this layer's Sturm bound.
Builds the compactified quotient Riemann surface that this layer specializes to congruence subgroups.

targets.target: Arithmetic specialization of the Fuchsian compact curve X(Gamma) to congruence subgroups, including cofiniteness
targets.note: Arithmetic groups act properly discontinuously, finite-index subgroups of PSL2(Z) have explicit fundamental domains (finite covolume follows from volume_fd_lt_top but is not stated), and free quotients carry charts; no compactification, no elliptic or cusp charts and no Riemann-surface structure on Gamma\H exist in either library.

targets.target: Cusps of Gamma identified with Gamma\P^1(Q); cusp count eps_inf and elliptic counts eps_2, eps_3 (with regular and irregular cusps)
targets.note: Cusps of SL2(Z) are P^1(Q), cusp orbits of arithmetic groups are finite, widths sum to the index, and stabilizer orders are computed; there is no count eps_inf, eps_2, eps_3 for Gamma0(N) or any congruence subgroup and no regular/irregular classification beyond infinity.

targets.target: The finite map X(Gamma) -> X(1) with degree [PSL2(Z) : Gamma-bar], consuming the generic fibre sum and Riemann-Hurwitz
targets.note: A set-level fibre count for Gamma\H -> SL2(Z)\H and index formulas for Gamma0(p^k) exist; there is no holomorphic map of compact curves, no degree theorem and no Riemann-Hurwitz.

duplicates.note: Constructs cusp orbits, widths and q-coordinates for cofinite Fuchsian groups, the generic form of the cusp data specialized here.
Proves the fibre-cardinality and degree formulas and cusp ramification e = w'/w for every finite-index inclusion, which contains the degree identification of this sublayer.

targets.target: Structure sheaf and divisor sheaves O_D on a compact Riemann surface, Cech H^0/H^1 with Leray's theorem and the local dbar-lemma, H^0(X,O) = C
targets.note: Holomorphic functions on a compact preconnected complex manifold are constant (H^0(X,O) = C), and Mathlib has a Cech complex functor and Ext-based sheaf cohomology; there is no structure sheaf on Riemann surfaces (Tau Ceti's holomorphicSheaf lives on C), no O_D, no Leray theorem and no dbar-lemma.

targets.target: Finiteness dim H^1(X, O_D) < infinity (Forster section 14)
targets.note: Only functional-analytic ingredients (Riesz theory of compact operators, open mapping theorem) exist.

targets.target: Analytic Riemann-Roch chi(O_D) = deg D + 1 - g on compact Riemann surfaces
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the algebraic Riemann-Roch theorem for function fields over a field k with exact constants (Stichtenoth's adelic route); nothing analytic, and the comparison with Riemann surfaces is not available.

targets.target: Meromorphic differentials, Serre duality H^1(O_D)^* = H^0(Omega_{-D}), dim H^0(Omega^1) = g, deg K = 2g - 2, residue theorem
targets.note: Only the function-field analogues exist (Weil differentials, deg of a canonical divisor = 2g - 2, regular differentials of dimension g, L(W - D) = Omega(D)).

targets.target: Analytic genus dim H^1(X,O) equals the topological genus (RiemannSurface.analyticGenus_eq_topologicalGenus), via Riemann-Hurwitz
targets.note: No topological genus of a surface, no degree of maps between compact Riemann surfaces and no Riemann-Hurwitz formula (only a combinatorial genus formula for permutation triples).

targets.target: X(1) = P^1 and genus X(1) = 0, with the j-function inputs
targets.note: No modular j-function and no compact X(1); only the algebraic statement that a genus-zero function field with a degree-one divisor is rational.

targets.target: Genus formula g = 1 + d/12 - eps_2/4 - eps_3/3 - eps_inf/2, S_2(Gamma) = H^0(X(Gamma), Omega^1) and dim S_2(Gamma) = g
targets.note: None of these statements exists.

duplicates.note: Owns topological genus, degree of finite holomorphic maps and Riemann-Hurwitz, which item (v) here consumes.
Owns the biholomorphism X(1) = P^1 that item (vi) consumes.
Identifies weight-two cusp forms with regular differentials on the compact modular curve (S_2 = H^0(Omega^1)).
Builds analytic coherent cohomology with local acyclicity via dbar/Cousin problems and Leray/Cech comparisons (on projective spaces), overlapping item (i).
States Riemann-Roch and Serre duality for curves in the algebraic setting; the roadmap explicitly does not identify it with the analytic version.

targets.target: The weight-k automorphy line bundle on X(Gamma) by local descent at elliptic points and cusps, with the floor-corrected divisor
targets.note: Only the algebraic invertible sheaf of a Weil divisor on a one-dimensional scheme exists; no automorphy sheaf and no identification of M_k with sections.

targets.target: Every holomorphic line bundle on a compact Riemann surface has a nonzero meromorphic section
targets.note: No holomorphic line bundles on Riemann surfaces in either library.

targets.target: Dimension formulas for M_k(Gamma), S_k(Gamma) at general level (D-S 3.5.1 even weight, 3.6.1 odd weight with the errata convention), weight-one bounds, and the degenerate weights k <= 0
targets.note: Only the level-one even-weight formula (Mathlib), dim M_0 = 1 and M_k = 0 for k < 0 on arithmetic groups, and vanishing in odd weight when -I is in Gamma exist; the general-level formulas, odd-weight regular/irregular bookkeeping and weight-one bounds are absent.

targets.target: Acceptance instances dim S_2(Gamma0(11)) = 1, dim S_2(Gamma0(23)) = 2, dim S_2(Gamma0(2)) = 0, dim M_2(Gamma0(11)) = 2, dim S_2(Gamma1(13)) = 2
targets.note: No dimension at level above one is computed.

duplicates.note: Identifies weight-k modular forms with sections of the k-th power of the Hodge line bundle on the (algebraic) modular curve.
Compares the Hodge bundle with the automorphy factor on the upper half-plane.

targets.target: Hurwitz class numbers H(D) by weighted counts of reduced positive-definite binary quadratic forms, with H 0 = -1/12 and the values H 3 = 1/3, H 4 = 1/2, H 7 = 1, H 8 = 1
targets.note: Neither library has reduction theory or class numbers of binary quadratic forms (hits for 'binary quadratic form' are positivity lemmas and a Legendre-symbol section); only ideal class numbers of number fields exist.

targets.target: Weight polynomials P_k(t,n) with generating function 1/(1 - tx + nx^2), the root-quotient formula and the relation with Chebyshev U
targets.note: The Dickson polynomials of the second kind satisfy exactly the P_k recurrence (dickson 2 n (k-2) evaluated at t is P_k(t,n)) and are related to Chebyshev U in Mathlib; the generating function, the root-quotient formula and the boundary value at t^2 = 4n are not stated.

targets.target: Eichler-Selberg trace formula for tr(T_n | S_k(SL2(Z))), even k >= 4
targets.note: No trace of any Hecke operator is computed.

targets.target: Period-polynomial space W_w = ker(1+S) cap ker(1+U+U^2), odd and extended even period maps, their Hecke equivariance and injectivity, dim W_w^+-, and M_k + S_k = W_w
targets.note: No period polynomials, Eichler-Shimura maps or SL2(Z)-action on homogeneous polynomials in either library.

targets.target: Popa-Zagier machinery: determinant-n matrix module and group ring with PSL2(Z) actions, the element T-tilde_n with its period and exchange relations, trace reduction and the conjugacy-type contributions
targets.note: Only double-coset Hecke rings exist; no group ring of determinant-n matrices and no Manin/Choie-Zagier elements.

targets.target: Correspondence between integer matrices of determinant n and trace t up to conjugacy and binary quadratic forms of discriminant t^2 - 4n
targets.note: Only disc(A) = tr^2 - 4 det for 2x2 matrices.

targets.target: Acceptance: tr T(1) = dim S_k, tr T(2) | S_12 = tau(2) = -24, charpoly of T_2 on S_k(SL2(Z))
targets.note: a_1(Delta) = 1 and dim S_12 = 1 exist; tau(2) = -24, Delta as a Hecke eigenform and the traces are absent.

AdditiveCombinatorics.summary: Mathlib already covers the elementary layer and more: sumsets, additive energy with the Cauchy-Schwarz bound, Plunnecke-Ruzsa, Ruzsa's triangle and covering lemmas, very small doubling, Freiman homomorphisms and approximate groups, characters of finite abelian groups, Roth's theorem (via corners and triangle removal, tower bound), Behrend's construction, van der Waerden via Hales-Jewett, Dirichlet's theorem and Chebyshev bounds. Tau Ceti adds only side results (graphon weak regularity, nilpotent unitriangular groups, a smoothed Wiener-Ikehara theorem). Genuinely missing are Fourier analysis on general finite abelian groups with Parseval, Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers, Freiman/PFR, Bohr sets and arithmetic regularity, Szemeredi's theorem for k >= 4 and the finite/infinite correspondence, Gowers norms and all nilsequence theory, the prime number theorem, the transference machinery and the Green-Tao theorem, and linear equations in primes with Mobius-nilsequence orthogonality.

targets.target: Sumsets, difference sets and iterated sumsets of finite sets
targets.note: Pointwise operations are stated multiplicatively with @[to_additive], giving Finset.add, Finset.sub and the iterated sumset n • s (scoped in Pointwise), with cardinality bounds such as card_add_le.

targets.target: Additive energy and the basic energy inequalities
targets.note: The additive versions are Finset.addEnergy (notation E[s,t]), the Cauchy-Schwarz bound #s^2 #t^2 <= #(s+t) E[s,t] (le_card_add_mul_addEnergy) and the representation-count formula; the trivial upper bound E(A,B) <= |A|^2|B| is not stated.

targets.target: Convolution and Fourier analysis on finite abelian groups (characters, inversion, Parseval/Plancherel, convolution to product), with normalized counting measure
targets.note: Characters of a finite abelian group form a basis with orthogonality, the discrete Fourier transform with inversion exists on ZMod N, Finset.expect gives normalized averages, and the representation-count convolution of finsets exists (additive name addConvolution); missing are a Fourier transform on general finite abelian groups, Parseval/Plancherel, and convolution of functions with its Fourier identity.

targets.target: Plunnecke-Ruzsa inequality, Ruzsa triangle inequality and Ruzsa covering
targets.note: All with @[to_additive] versions (#(mB - nB) <= K^{m+n}|A| for A nonempty in a commutative group, the subtraction triangle inequality, covering, doubling constants sigma[A,B], small tripling); cardinality hypotheses are explicit.

duplicates.note: Constructs additive characters and their orthogonality, overlapping the character side of the finite Fourier analysis asked for here.

targets.target: Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers theorem
targets.note: No BSG in either library (searches for balog, BSG, Gowers and uses of energy outside Energy.lean); only its inputs (energy bounds, Plunnecke-Ruzsa) exist.

targets.target: Source-scoped Freiman-type inverse results (Freiman homomorphisms, small doubling structure, Freiman-Ruzsa in bounded torsion, polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa)
targets.note: Very small doubling (< 3/2 and < 2) structure theorems (multiplicative only), Freiman homomorphisms, approximate groups from small tripling and Cauchy-Davenport exist; Freiman's theorem, Ruzsa's torsion version, Kneser's theorem and PFR are absent.

targets.target: Bohr sets with size bounds and regularity
targets.note: No Bohr sets (the only 'bohr' hits are Bohr-Mollerup).

targets.target: Regularity and density increments with quantitative losses (arithmetic regularity, energy/density increment, Chang-type lemmas)
targets.note: Graph regularity with energy increments, the dissociated-span lemma (additive version) and graphon weak regularity exist; Green's arithmetic regularity lemma, Fourier density increments and Chang's lemma are absent.

targets.target: Roth's theorem (3-term progressions) in finite and integer form with a quantified density
targets.note: Proved via corners and triangle removal with a tower-type bound (cornersTheoremBound), in any finite abelian group and in [n]; ThreeAPFree is the additive form of ThreeGPFree.

targets.target: Szemeredi's theorem for progressions of every length k (and van der Waerden)
targets.note: Only the colouring statements exist (Hales-Jewett and a monochromatic homothetic copy, i.e. van der Waerden); the density theorem for k >= 4 is absent.

targets.target: Arithmetic removal through a selected proof route (graph/hypergraph removal, arithmetic removal lemma)
targets.note: Triangle removal (and its corners application) exists; general graph removal, hypergraph removal and Green's arithmetic removal lemma are absent.

targets.target: Ergodic and combinatorial infrastructure as owned prerequisites (Furstenberg correspondence, multiple recurrence)
targets.note: Poincare recurrence, Bergelson's intersectivity lemma and the mean ergodic theorem exist; the Furstenberg correspondence principle and multiple recurrence are absent.

targets.target: Proved correspondence between finite quantitative and infinite positive-density forms (Varnavides supersaturation)
targets.note: No Varnavides argument and no upper or Banach density; only Schnirelmann density exists.

targets.target: Gowers uniformity norms U^d (inner product, positivity, Gowers-Cauchy-Schwarz, monotonicity)
targets.note: No Gowers norms or cube averages in either library.

targets.target: Generalized von Neumann estimates
targets.note: Only graph counting lemmas exist (triangle counting, the graphon counting lemma), not additive counting operators controlled by U^d.

targets.target: Inverse theorems for Gowers norms in their proved settings (finite fields, cyclic groups, Green-Tao-Ziegler)
targets.note: Absent, including the U^2 Fourier inverse theorem.

targets.target: Nilmanifolds, polynomial sequences, nilsequences and their complexity
targets.note: Only nilpotent groups, Lie groups and the unitriangular filtration exist; no nilmanifolds, Mal'cev bases, filtered polynomial sequences or nilsequences.

targets.target: Pseudorandom majorants satisfying the linear forms and correlation conditions (W-trick, Goldston-Yildirim truncated divisor sum)
targets.note: Only Selberg Lambda^2 upper-bound sieve weights exist; no pseudorandom measure, linear forms or correlation condition, W-trick or truncated divisor sum.

targets.target: Dense model theorem, relative counting and relative Szemeredi theorem
targets.note: Absent; only generic Hahn-Banach separation is available.

targets.target: Green-Tao theorem: the primes contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions
targets.note: Not even three-term progressions in the primes.

targets.target: Prime-distribution inputs of the proof: the prime number theorem, Dirichlet's theorem and the classical zero-free region
targets.note: Dirichlet's theorem (qualitative), Chebyshev bounds and nonvanishing of Dirichlet L-functions on Re s >= 1 exist; the prime number theorem, its version in progressions and a quantitative zero-free region are absent from both libraries (Tau Ceti has only a smoothed Wiener-Ikehara theorem and conditional transfers).

duplicates.note: Selberg sieve weights, of which the Goldston-Yildirim truncated divisor sum used for the majorant is a variant.

targets.target: Finite-complexity systems of linear equations in primes with local factors, excluding proportional degeneracies
targets.note: No linear-equations-in-primes asymptotic, singular series, Hardy-Littlewood tuples or three-primes theorem, as theorems or hypotheses.

targets.target: Mobius-nilsequence orthogonality
targets.note: Only the Mobius function and its L-series exist; no Mobius sum estimates, not even o(x).

targets.target: Admissibility and finite (Cauchy-Schwarz) complexity of systems of affine-linear forms
targets.note: No systems of linear forms or complexity notions.

duplicates.note: Constructs singular series and local densities, the local factors of the linear-patterns asymptotic.
Sums-of-primes theorems by the circle method, overlapping the simplest linear patterns in primes.
Multiplicative-function correlations and Sarnak-type statements, overlapping Mobius orthogonality.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCodingTh.summary: Tau Ceti has only the start of coding theory: the LinearCode/AdditiveCode aliases and a generator and parity-check matrix API (rank formulas, existence of generator matrices, row counts), while Mathlib supplies Hamming weight and distance, the dot-product form with general orthogonal-complement theory, and primitive additive characters of finite fields. The lattice half is largely in place through Tau Ceti's integral-lattice library: coordinate powers of finite bilinear and quadratic modules with orthogonal complements, discriminant forms, the overlattice-isotropic-subgroup correspondence with A_{L_H} = H^perp/H, and the A_n and D_n discriminant forms. Genuinely missing are everything code-specific beyond matrix presentations: minimum distance, puncturing, shortening and direct sums, code equivalences, Euclidean and Hermitian dual codes, weight enumerators and MacWilliams, doubly-even and Type II theory, the tetracode, hexacode and Golay codes, Construction A, and the identification of codes with isotropic subgroups of the discriminant group of m Z^iota.

targets.target: Linear and additive code aliases over arbitrary finite coordinate types with the inherited Submodule/AddSubgroup operations, and #C = q^dim C
targets.note: The aliases are abbrevs for Submodule F (iota -> F) and AddSubgroup (iota -> A), so membership, ext and the lattice operations are Mathlib's; the cardinality formula is Mathlib's general card V = card K ^ finrank. No code-specific restatements exist.

targets.target: Codes generated and checked by a matrix, generator/parity-check predicates, existence from bases, row-span and syndrome criteria, rank/dimension formulas, row counts k and n-k, invariance under invertible row operations, generator of C = check matrix of C^perp
targets.note: Tau Ceti has checkedBy and IsParityCheckMatrix (lines 50, 68), membership criteria, finrank = rank and card - rank, existence of a full-rank generator matrix, both row counts, and generatedBy <= checkedBy iff H * G^T = 0. Missing: invariance of the generated code under invertible row operations, deletion of dependent rows, existence of parity-check matrices, and the generator/dual-code check-matrix statement (no dual code is defined).

targets.target: Systematic form relative to an information set: [I | A] and [-A^T | I] generate and check orthogonal codes
targets.note: Only row-echelon and kernel-basis machinery exists; no block-matrix systematic forms or information sets.

targets.target: Puncturing and shortening on retained coordinates, with membership, dimension, repeated-operation and reindexing lemmas and deleted-coordinate bounds
targets.note: Only restriction of functions along a map exists; no puncture or shorten operation.

targets.target: Direct sum of codes on disjoint-union coordinates with membership, dimension, cardinality, Hamming, associativity and commutativity statements
targets.note: Only the coordinate equivalence (Pi over S + T) = product exists.

targets.target: Permutation, monomial and semilinear equivalences of words and codes, their stabilizer (automorphism) groups, and preservation of dimension, weight, distance and weight enumerator
targets.note: Only invariance of Hamming distance under coordinatewise injective maps exists; no code equivalences or automorphism groups.

duplicates.note: Develops evaluation and residue codes with encoding maps, dimension and distance bounds, which needs the same linear-code carrier API.

targets.target: Hamming support, weight and distance: relation with Function.support, support formulae for sums and scalars, weight <= length, dist(x,y) = wt(y - x)
targets.note: Mathlib has weight, distance, dist = wt(-x + y), the length bound and smul/triangle lemmas; the link to Function.support and the support formulae for sums are not stated.

targets.target: Minimum distance of linear and additive codes (zero-code convention), attainment, equality with least pairwise distance, invariance under isometries, puncturing, shortening and direct-sum bounds
targets.note: No minimum distance is defined in either library (the phrase occurs only in the Hamming.lean docstring).

targets.target: Standard dot-product form, its nondegeneracy, the Euclidean dual C^perp via BilinForm.orthogonal, (C^perp)^perp = C, dim C + dim C^perp = n, #C * #C^perp = q^n, self-orthogonal and self-dual characterizations
targets.note: The general orthogonal-complement theory for a nondegenerate reflexive form and the perfect-pairing instance for the dot product exist; there is no dual code, no packaged nondegeneracy of the dot form as a BilinForm, no #C * #C^perp = q^n over a field and no self-orthogonal/self-dual predicates for linear codes.

targets.target: Duality with puncturing, shortening and direct sums: (puncture C s)^perp = shorten C^perp s, (shorten C s)^perp = puncture C^perp s, (C + D)^perp = C^perp + D^perp
targets.note: Puncture and shorten do not exist; only the product formula for orthogonal complements in finite bilinear modules.

targets.target: Hermitian duality over a finite field with an involutive automorphism: membership, nondegeneracy, double dual, dimension, rowspan(G) = C iff ker(sigma(G)) = C^perp_H, Frobenius on F4
targets.note: Only the generic sesquilinear orthogonal (with an inclusion into its double orthogonal) and Frobenius exist; no Hermitian dual code.

targets.target: Coordinate power of a finite bilinear alphabet, orthogonal additive codes with cardinality and double-perpendicular results under nondegeneracy, and the coordinate finite quadratic module
targets.note: The coordinate power is nondegenerate when the alphabet is (IsNondegenerate.coordinatePower, line 101), and the cardinality and double-perp theorems hold for every nondegenerate finite bilinear module, hence for the coordinate power.

duplicates.note: Its code layer needs dimension and distance statements for linear codes (BCH/Reed-Solomon), overlapping minimum distance and duality here.

targets.target: Weight distribution A_w(C) and the one-variable and homogeneous weight enumerators with coefficient formulae, evaluation at (1,1), direct-sum product and recovery of minimum distance
targets.note: No weight distribution or enumerator in either library (searches for weight enumerator, weightDistribution, enumerator).

targets.target: Finite-character orthogonality for a subspace and its dual, sum over c in C of psi(<c,x>) = #C [x in C^perp], using the primitive additive character of a finite field, as reusable Fourier API
targets.note: Primitive additive characters of finite fields, the vanishing of nontrivial character sums and dual orthogonality on finite abelian groups exist; the subspace/dual-code orthogonality lemma and a finite Fourier transform on iota -> F are absent.

targets.target: q-ary MacWilliams identity #C * W_{C^perp}(X,Y) = W_C(X+(q-1)Y, X-Y), its normalized and Krawtchouk forms, and invariance for self-dual codes
targets.note: No MacWilliams identity and no Krawtchouk polynomials in either library.

duplicates.note: Constructs additive characters of finite fields and their orthogonality relations, the character input of the MacWilliams proof.

targets.target: Even, doubly-even, self-orthogonal, self-dual and Type II predicates; doubly-even binary codes are self-orthogonal
targets.note: Self-orthogonality exists only as isotropy in finite bilinear modules; no code predicates and no wt(x + y) = wt x + wt y - 2|x and y| identity.

targets.target: Binary self-dual codes: all weights even, all-ones word in the code, dimension n/2, 2^{n/2} words; Type II codes have length divisible by 8
targets.note: Only #H^2 = #A for Lagrangian subgroups of nondegenerate finite bilinear modules (which would give #C = 2^{n/2}); nothing on binary codes or length mod 8.

targets.target: Closure of doubly-even and Type II codes under direct sums and coordinate permutations
targets.note: Direct sums and code equivalences are themselves absent (Layer 1).

targets.target: Type II weight-enumerator invariances W_C(X+Y, X-Y) = 2^{n/2} W_C(X,Y) and W_C(X, iY) = W_C(X,Y)
targets.note: No weight enumerators; Gleason hits in Mathlib are unrelated topology.

targets.target: Ternary tetracode [4,2,3] over ZMod 3: Euclidean self-dual, all nonzero weights 3, W = X^4 + 8XY^3
targets.note: No tetracode in either library.

targets.target: Hexacode [6,3,4] over F4: Hermitian self-dual, weights 0, 4, 6, W = X^6 + 45X^2Y^4 + 18Y^6, and the permutation equivalence with its Frobenius conjugate
targets.note: No hexacode; GaloisField 2 2 is not used in either library.

targets.target: Extended binary Golay code G24 from [I12 | B]: rank 12, minimum distance 8, self-dual, doubly even, weight enumerator 1 + 759 + 2576 + 759 + 1; punctured [23,12,7] code and re-extension
targets.note: No Golay code; Tau Ceti's Mathieu-group files only transcribe presentations of M11-M24.

targets.target: Extended ternary Golay code G12 from [I6 | A]: [12,6,6], self-dual, weights divisible by 3, W = X^12 + 264X^6Y^6 + 440X^3Y^9 + 24Y^12
targets.note: No ternary Golay code.

targets.target: Construction A lattice P_m(C) with form B_m on Q^iota: full lattice for every C, integral exactly when C <= C^perp, and the carrier identity P_m(C)^dual = P_m(C^perp)
targets.note: D_n = {x in Z^n : sum x_i even} is the unscaled Construction A of the even-weight binary code but is defined by coordinates; the general overlattice duality dual(L_H) = L_{H^perp} exists, but no Construction A lattice from a code.

targets.target: disc(P_m(C)) = m^{#iota}/(#C)^2 for self-orthogonal C, and p^{n-2k} for linear [n,k] codes over ZMod p
targets.note: The general index formula disc(L_H) * |H|^2 = disc L would give the code formula once m Z^iota and its discriminant group are identified (Layer 7), but no code version is stated.

targets.target: Unimodular iff C = C^perp; q_m and even iff q_m vanishes on C; odd m never even; q_2(c) = wt(c)/4 so even iff doubly even; Type II codes give even unimodular lattices, applied to G24
targets.note: The general gluing criteria (self-dual iff Lagrangian, even iff quadratic-isotropic) exist and E8 is built as D8 glued by a spinor class, not by Construction A from the Hamming code; no Type II code theorem and no G24 lattice.

targets.target: Type II codes over Z/2^r and their even unimodular lattices; naturality under coordinate permutations and signed coordinate changes
targets.note: Only general lattice isometries exist.

targets.target: L0(m,iota) = m Z^iota with form B_m: L0^dual = Z^iota and an isometry of its discriminant module with (ZMod m)^iota carrying the pairing to sum lift(x_i)lift(y_i)/m, and q_m for even m
targets.note: Dual lattices of Gram-matrix lattices on Z^iota, the rank-one discriminant group ZMod |2m| and cyclic finite quadratic modules exist; the scaled lattice m Z^iota with form (1/m) dot and its discriminant identification do not (scale only multiplies forms by integers).

targets.target: Transport of an additive code C to an AddSubgroup of the discriminant group; its orthogonal complement is the preimage of C^perp, bilinear isotropy iff C <= C^perp, quadratic isotropy iff q_m vanishes on C, and ofIsotropicSubgroup is isometric to P_m(C)
targets.note: Isotropy of a subgroup of a coordinate power is characterized coordinatewise, but nothing connects codes, m Z^iota or Construction A.

targets.target: Gluing: A_{P_m(C)} = C^perp/C as bilinear and (for even m, q_m|C = 0) quadratic modules on the actual subtype quotient, and unimodularity from the Lagrangian condition
targets.note: The general gluing theorem this layer consumes is proved for nondegenerate integral lattices (A_{L_H} = H^perp/H bilinear, and quadratic for even L; L_H self-dual iff H Lagrangian); its instance for codes is missing because m Z^iota and the code transport are.

targets.target: Other discriminant alphabets: coordinate powers and coordinatewise isometries, the A2 alphabet (q(a) = a^2/3), the D4 alphabet identified with F4, and the checks that the tetracode and G12 are Lagrangian for A2 and the hexacode for D4
targets.note: The A_n and even-D_n discriminant forms are identified with explicit models (n = 2 gives q(k) = k^2/3; n = 4 gives the Klein four-group with q = 1/2 on nonzero classes), and coordinate powers of finite quadratic modules with coordinatewise isometries exist; the F4 identification of the D4 alphabet and the tetracode, G12 and hexacode Lagrangian checks are absent.

targets.target: Reusable interface: isometry from a coordinate finite quadratic module to the discriminant module of an orthogonal lattice sum
targets.note: Only the two-summand isometry A_{L perp M} = A_L x A_M exists; there are no finite lattice powers and no identification with a coordinate power.

duplicates.note: States the overlattice-isotropic-subgroup correspondence and A_{L_H} = H^perp/H with Lagrangian iff unimodular, the general theorem this layer specializes.
Computes the A_n and D_n discriminant forms, which include the A2 and D4 alphabets used here.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/DenseGraphLimits.summary: Most of the roadmap is already in Tau Ceti: graphons, homomorphism densities, cut norm and the cross-carrier coupling cut distance with its triangle inequality, GraphonSpace, the counting lemma, Frieze-Kannan weak regularity with the partition energy, density of step graphons, the AEEqFun view, the coupling/map agreement, forward separation, Goodman, Mantel and Sidorenko for C4, the labeled-graph and connection-matrix predicates, the whole finite and joint sampling layer, exchangeable graph laws with dissociation, and the exposure/McDiarmid concentration engine; Mathlib already has the measure-preserving representation from [0,1] that Layer 5 plans to build. Genuinely missing are completeness and compactness of GraphonSpaceI (only total boundedness is there), the atomless mod-null equivalence, the inverse counting lemma with the separation and convergence equivalences, associativity of gluing, the whole Lovasz-Szegedy representability theorem and its Moebius spine, the extremality, infinite-law and graphon-mixture representation of exchangeable graph laws, and the second sampling lemma and almost-sure sampling convergence.

targets.target: Sym2-indexed finite products for edge densities
targets.note: Edge factors are defined on Sym2 V through Sym2.lift, with measurability, bounds and integrability of products over edge Finsets; Mathlib has no multiplicative Sym2 product lemma, which Tau Ceti avoids by taking products over F.edgeFinset.

targets.target: Curry/uncurry lemmas for product measures and Measure.pi
targets.note: Coordinate-pair and restriction maps are measure-preserving for finite Measure.pi, two-coordinate Fubini and Mathlib's reindexing/splitting equivalences exist; a measure-preserving curry/uncurry for a finite Measure.pi is not stated in either library (only for infinitePi).

targets.target: Standard-Borel plumbing
targets.note: Products of standard Borel spaces, Borel isomorphisms and the representation of a probability measure as a pushforward of Lebesgue measure on [0,1] are in Mathlib; Tau Ceti repackages the latter as a MeasurePreserving map without Nonempty.

targets.target: Symmetric-kernel R-module and the Graphon structure on it
targets.note: SymmKernel carries AddCommGroup and Module R instances (Kernel/Basic.lean:189, 193); Graphon extends it with values in [0,1] over a probability carrier.

targets.target: homDensity t(F,W) with t in [0,1], the constant-graphon value p^{e(F)}, explicit edge and triangle integrals, multiplicativity over disjoint unions, and t(F, W_G) = hom(F,G)/|V(G)|^{|V(F)|}
targets.note: Bounds are homDensity_nonneg/homDensity_le_one (Basic.lean:191, 195) and the edge density integral is line 332 of SmallGraphs.lean.

targets.target: cutNorm with seminorm laws, the L1 bound and the set form sup_{S,T} |int_{S x T} W|
targets.note: The seminorm laws are separate lemmas (zero, neg, add, sub, smul) rather than a bundled Seminorm.

targets.target: Coupling-primary cross-carrier cutDist with IsCoupling and overlayDiff, and its triangle inequality on arbitrary probability carriers
targets.note: The triangle inequality holds on three arbitrary probability carriers (Janson Lemma 6.5); symmetry and cutDist_self are in Distance.lean.

targets.target: Fixed-carrier metric quotient GraphonSpace Omega mu and the canonical GraphonSpaceI
targets.note: Defined as the SeparationQuotient of the pseudometric space, whose MetricSpace instance is Mathlib's.

targets.target: Acceptance objects: a finite graph as a step graphon, one-edge and triangle densities
targets.note: Step graphons over measurable finite partitions and the 0/1 graphon of a finite graph on m equal cells of [0,1].

duplicates.note: Proves the gluing lemma for couplings that the cut-distance triangle inequality rests on.

targets.target: Forward counting lemma |t(F,U) - t(F,W)| <= e(F) ||U - W||_cut and its coupling form
targets.note: Same-carrier, coupling and cut-distance forms, carriers arbitrary.

targets.target: Descent homDensityOnSpace of t(F, -) to GraphonSpace
targets.note: Lipschitz with constant e(F) on every fixed-carrier GraphonSpace.

targets.target: Frieze-Kannan weak regularity over measurable Finpartitions with complexity 4^{ceil(1/eps^2)+1}
targets.note: The block-averaged step graphon is within eps in cut norm on a measurable partition with at most 4^{ceil(1/eps^2)+1} parts, the migration baseline.

targets.target: Block averages stepGraphonAvg, graphonPartitionEnergy, the L2 Pythagoras increment and monotonicity/nonnegativity
targets.note: Not yet identified with MeasureTheory.condExp, which the roadmap defers to Layer 3/4.

targets.target: Density of step graphons in cut distance
targets.note: Any carrier.

targets.target: Total boundedness of (GraphonSpace, delta_cut)
targets.note: Proved for the canonical carrier GraphonSpaceI (through standard-Borel models on [0,1]); not stated for GraphonSpace over an arbitrary carrier.

targets.target: Round trip between graphons and AEEqFun classes: toAEEqFun and a measurable-representative section back
targets.note: The way back is an existence theorem characterizing which classes come from graphons rather than a named section function.

targets.target: Invariance theorems homDensity_congr_ae, cutNorm_congr_ae, cutDist_eq_zero_of_aeEq
targets.note: Under the pinned names; cutDist_congr_ae_left/right add full a.e. invariance across carriers.

targets.target: Lovasz-Szegedy compactness: CompactSpace GraphonSpaceI and CompleteSpace GraphonSpaceI
targets.note: Only the totally-bounded half exists; completeness, and hence the CompactSpace and CompleteSpace instances, are absent.

targets.target: Analytic inputs: measure-preserving realignment of cut-Cauchy sequences and dyadic conditional-expectation/martingale L1-Cauchy approximation
targets.note: Mathlib's martingale convergence (Levy upward) is available, but no realignment or martingale approximation of graphons exists.

targets.target: Every standard Borel probability space receives a measure-preserving map from ([0,1], volume) (Janson A.9), atoms allowed
targets.note: Mathlib already proves the pushforward representation for standard Borel spaces (with Nonempty), which the roadmap asks to build; Tau Ceti states it as MeasurePreserving under the pinned name, declared in Mathlib's namespace.

targets.target: Atomless mod-null measure-preserving equivalence with the unit interval (exists_mpModNull_equiv_unitInterval)
targets.note: Only Borel isomorphisms without measures exist; Pullback/Basic.lean records that the mod-null equivalence is not built.

targets.target: Map form cutDistPullback and cutDist_eq_cutDistPullback over standard Borel carriers
targets.note: Both carriers standard Borel, atoms allowed.

targets.target: Forward separation: cutDist U W = 0 implies t(F,U) = t(F,W) for all F, cross-carrier, with the same-carrier corollary
targets.note: Arbitrary carriers, all graphs on Fin n; the same-carrier form is the special case, not separately named.

targets.target: Inverse counting lemma cutDist_eq_zero_of_forall_homDensity_eq_cross (carrier-free), via exists_graphon_unitInterval_cutDist_eq_zero
targets.note: The representation on [0,1] is proved only for standard Borel carriers; the inverse counting lemma itself is absent.

targets.target: Separation iff cutDist_eq_zero_iff_forall_homDensity_eq_cross and graphonSpace_ext_homDensity
targets.note: Only the forward direction and the quotient equality criterion exist.

targets.target: Convergence equivalence tendsto_graphonSpace_iff_forall_homDensity with continuous_homDensityOnSpace
targets.note: The easy direction (continuity of each descended density) exists; the equivalence, which needs compactness and inverse counting, does not.

targets.target: Goodman, Mantel and Sidorenko for C4 as graphon inequalities
targets.note: Mathlib also has Turan's theorem for finite graphs (Extremal/Turan.lean), which gives the finite Mantel bound.

targets.target: W-random sampling expectation E[t(F, G(n,W))] -> t(F,W)
targets.note: Exact unbiasedness of the injective density and the C(k,2)/n closeness bound are public; the limit statement is not (the explicit bound for the ordinary density is only a private lemma).

targets.target: Concrete rational density checks
k-labeled graphs with injective labels, gluing that returns a k-labeled graph, forgetLabels, and the gluing algebra laws (associativity and commutativity up to isomorphism)
targets.note: Commutativity up to isomorphism preserving labels is proved; associativity up to isomorphism is absent.

targets.target: GraphParam, IsIsoInvariant, connectionMatrix, IsReflectionPositive over Fin n families, IsMultiplicative, IsNormalized
targets.note: Each predicate has a real body; IsReflectionPositive.posSemidef extends PSD to any finite index type.

targets.target: lovasz_szegedy_representability: a graph parameter is t(-, W) for a graphon on ([0,1], volume) iff iso-invariant, multiplicative, normalized and reflection-positive
targets.note: Neither direction is stated: even the easy direction (t(-, W) satisfies the four predicates) is only available through ingredients such as homDensity_sum and homDensity_eq_of_iso.

targets.target: Derived corollary graphParam_mem_Icc_of_representability_axioms
targets.note: Only nonnegativity on self-gluings and f(n, bot) = 1 for multiplicative normalized parameters.

targets.target: Proof spine: graphParamMobius_nonneg, graphParamMobius_sum_eq_one, graphParamMobius_sum_comap, paramGraphLaw, paramExchangeableLaw with its upper masses and dissociation
targets.note: None of the Moebius-transform declarations exist; the Layer-9b bridge isDissociated_iff_upperMass_mul and the upper-mass sampling anchor that the spine consumes are already proved, and a finite-order measure extensionality lemma supplies the Moebius inversion step.

targets.target: W-random graph law sampleGraph W n on SimpleGraph (Fin n)
targets.note: A probability measure built from the PMF of sample masses, on Mathlib's measurable structure on SimpleGraph.

targets.target: Compatibility sampleGraph (Graphon.const p) n = binomial random graph G(Fin n, p)
targets.note: Recovers Mathlib's binomialRandom exactly.

targets.target: Finite estimators homDensityFin and injHomDensity, the closeness bound |t - t0| <= C(k,2)/n and unbiasedness E[t0(F, G(n,W))] = t(F,W)
targets.note: Unbiasedness needs card V <= m; the injective density uses the falling-factorial denominator.

targets.target: Joint sampling object infiniteSampleLaw W with infiniteSampleLaw_map_restrictFin
targets.note: One probability space with i.i.d. positions and one uniform coin per pair; every finite marginal is sampleGraph W n.

targets.target: ExchangeableGraphLaw, sampleExchangeableLaw with sampleGraph_map_comap, upperMass and upperMass_sampleExchangeableLaw
targets.note: Consistency along every label injection; upper masses determine the law (ext_upperMass).

targets.target: IsDissociated, isDissociated_sampleExchangeableLaw and the extremality theorem exists_graphon_of_isDissociated
targets.note: Dissociation, its upper-mass characterization and dissociation of sampling laws are proved; the extremality theorem that dissociated laws are graphon sampling laws is absent.

targets.target: InfiniteExchangeableGraphLaw and the finite-infinite extension exchangeableGraphLawEquivInfinite
targets.note: Only a generic countable projective-limit (Kolmogorov extension) theorem exists.

targets.target: Existence spine: mixtureExchangeableLaw, empiricalMixing, the collision estimate, compactness extraction, limit identification, uniqueness, mixtureExchangeableLawEquiv and the Dirac/dissociated characterization
targets.note: None of the named declarations exist, GraphonSpace has no measurable structure, and the compactness input (Layer 4) is missing; Mathlib's CompactSpace (ProbabilityMeasure E) instance (Prokhorov.lean:176) and Tau Ceti's sequence de Finetti correspondence are the nearest analogues.

targets.target: Summit graphonMixtureLawEquiv with its Dirac and upper-mass anchors, and infiniteSampleLaw_eq_extension
targets.note: Absent (searches for graphonMixtureLawEquiv, infiniteSampleLaw_eq_extension, mixture).

targets.target: Graph/array law-level interface: EdgeIndex, graphCoordEquiv with measurability, graphCoordEquiv_comap, and graphLawArrayLawEquiv
targets.note: The carrier-level contract exists; the law-level equivalence graphLawArrayLawEquiv is absent, and Tau Ceti's Aldous-Hoover development has only the easy (coding implies exchangeable) direction.

duplicates.note: Owns exchangeable arrays and the Aldous-Hoover representation, whose symmetric Boolean case is the graph-law mixture representation, and finite de Finetti bounds of the same (m choose 2)/n shape as the collision estimate.

targets.target: Second sampling lemma in probability, delta_cut(G(n,W), W) -> 0, and infiniteSampleLaw_tendstoInMeasure_cutDist
targets.note: The sampling files never mention cutDist or finiteGraphGraphon.

targets.target: Almost-sure convergence infiniteSampleLaw_ae_tendsto_cutDist
targets.note: The Borel-Cantelli summability input exists, but no almost-sure convergence statement for densities or cut distance.

targets.target: Padded vertex exposure: exposureMeasure, exposedSample, map_exposedSample, abs_homDensityFin_exposedSample_update_le
targets.note: The law identification makes the exposure a genuine representation of sampleGraph W n.

targets.target: McDiarmid concentration sampleGraph_homDensityFin_concentration and summability tsum_sampleGraph_homDensityFin_tail_ne_top for Borel-Cantelli
targets.note: McDiarmid is Tau Ceti's (sub-Gaussian MGF form for identically distributed coordinates); Mathlib supplies Borel-Cantelli.
